## ExcelBridge: Enterprise Inventory & Procurement Migration Platform

**Document Version:** 1.0.0

## 1. Executive Summary & Strategic Context

### 1.1 Problem Statement

Enterprise organizations managing inventory and procurement operations via Excel workbooks represent the single largest addressable market segment for B2B SaaS migration. These organizations are characterized by:

- **Operational fragility:** Business continuity depends on key individuals who maintain institutional knowledge of workbook logic, hidden formulas, tab dependencies, and undocumented calculation chains.
- **Collaboration collapse:** Concurrent editing, version conflicts, and emailed attachments create data integrity failures that manifest as stockouts, duplicate purchase orders, and financial reporting errors.
- **Scale ceiling:** Excel's row limit (1,048,576 rows), memory constraints, and single-threaded calculation engine create hard operational boundaries that growing enterprises routinely breach.
- **Audit impossibility:** No native change log, no field-level audit trail, and no separation of duties means regulatory compliance (SOX, ISO 9001, FDA 21 CFR Part 11) requires expensive manual reconciliation.

### 1.2 Market Context

Target segment: Mid-market to enterprise organizations (200–10,000 employees) with annual procurement spend between $5M–$500M. Primary verticals: Manufacturing, Distribution, Healthcare Supply Chain, Retail/CPG, Aerospace & Defense.

The core competitive differentiator is **migration confidence**: the demonstrable ability to import an organization's existing Excel workbooks with sufficient fidelity that users can verify correctness before committing to the new system, run both systems in parallel, and retain a bidirectional data bridge for the first 90–180 days post-migration.

### 1.3 Strategic Objectives

| Objective | Metric | Target |
|---|---|---|
| Migration completion rate | % of customers who complete full cutover | ≥ 75% within 6 months of contract |
| Time to first value | Days from contract sign to first successful data import | ≤ 3 business days |
| Data fidelity | % of data rows imported without error requiring manual correction | ≥ 95% |
| Customer retention at 12 months | Net Revenue Retention | ≥ 120% |
| Support burden | Support tickets per migration | ≤ 5 per customer |

---

## 2. MVP Scope & User Journey

### 2.1 MVP Definition

The MVP delivers a complete, self-service migration path for a single organizational unit (one department, one facility, or one product line) from Excel to the SaaS platform. Multi-site, multi-ERP integration, and advanced automation are explicitly deferred to post-MVP phases.

**MVP Boundaries:**
- Maximum file size: 50 MB per workbook, 10 workbooks per migration project
- Maximum row count: 500,000 rows across all imported files in a single project
- Supported file formats: .xlsx, .xls (Excel 97-2003), .csv, .tsv
- Supported browsers: Chrome 110+, Firefox 115+, Edge 110+ (Safari 16+ best-effort)
- No native desktop application in MVP; browser-only

### 2.2 Persona Definitions

**Primary Personas:**

**P1 — The Excel Champion (Protagonist)**
- Title: Operations Manager, Supply Chain Analyst, Procurement Specialist
- Technical profile: Advanced Excel user; understands VLOOKUP, pivot tables, named ranges; no programming experience
- Goal: Validate that the new system handles "their" workbooks correctly without losing data or breaking workflows
- Fear: Being blamed when something breaks after migration
- Critical success factor: Must see their data in the new system and confirm it looks right before anyone else uses it

**P2 — The IT Gatekeeper**
- Title: IT Director, Systems Administrator, Enterprise Architect
- Technical profile: Understands data security, SSO, file formats, API concepts
- Goal: Ensure migration doesn't create security vulnerabilities, data exfiltration risks, or compliance gaps
- Fear: Shadow IT, data residency violations, unsanctioned integrations
- Critical success factor: Must approve data handling policy, encryption standards, and access controls before any data is uploaded

**P3 — The Executive Sponsor**
- Title: VP Supply Chain, Chief Procurement Officer, COO
- Technical profile: Dashboard consumer; not hands-on with data
- Goal: Reduce operational risk, improve reporting capability, achieve cost savings from better procurement visibility
- Fear: Project overrun, user adoption failure, disruption to operations
- Critical success factor: Progress dashboard showing migration health, time-to-value projections, and risk indicators

**P4 — The Migration Success Manager (Internal)**
- Title: Customer Success Manager (CSM) at the vendor
- Technical profile: Familiar with the product; can read basic SQL and understand data structures
- Goal: Drive customers to full cutover; reduce churn
- Critical success factor: Real-time visibility into customer migration progress; ability to intervene proactively at drop-off points

### 2.3 End-to-End MVP User Journey

The user journey is organized into six discrete phases. Each phase has a defined entry state, exit state, and success gate.

---

#### Phase 0: Pre-Migration Discovery (Days 1–3)

**Entry:** Contract signed; customer admin account provisioned.

**Journey Steps:**

```
1. Customer admin receives welcome email with provisioned tenant URL
   └─ Email contains: onboarding guide PDF, video walkthrough link,
      CSM calendar link, and "Start Migration" CTA button

2. Admin logs in (SSO or email/password)
   └─ First-time login triggers: MFA enrollment, data processing
      agreement acceptance, tenant configuration wizard

3. Tenant Configuration Wizard (5 screens, ~10 minutes):
   Screen 1: Organization profile (name, industry, country, primary currency)
   Screen 2: Data residency selection (US-East, EU-West, APAC)
   Screen 3: IT security review checklist (encryption confirmation,
             IP allowlist configuration, SSO setup or deferral)
   Screen 4: Team member invitation (add up to 5 users with role selection)
   Screen 5: Migration project creation (name, description, scope definition)

4. System generates: Migration Project ID, dedicated CSM assignment,
   onboarding timeline with milestone dates
```

**Exit State:** Active tenant with at least one migration project created and at least two users invited (admin + one Excel Champion).

**Success Gate:** Admin has completed tenant setup AND at least one additional team member has accepted their invitation within 48 hours.

---

#### Phase 1: Workbook Inventory & Upload (Days 3–7)

**Entry:** Active migration project; at least one user with Migrator role.

**Journey Steps:**

```
1. Excel Champion navigates to "Import Workbooks" within migration project

2. File Discovery Assistant:
   └─ System presents: "Tell us about your workbooks" questionnaire
      Q1: How many active workbooks do you use for inventory tracking?
      Q2: How many for purchase orders/requisitions?
      Q3: Do any workbooks pull data from other workbooks (linked files)?
      Q4: What is your approximate total row count? (rough estimate)
   └─ Answers shape the import strategy recommendation

3. Workbook Upload:
   └─ Drag-and-drop or file picker
   └─ Up to 10 files simultaneously
   └─ Real-time upload progress with file validation (format check, size check)
   └─ Virus/malware scan (ClamAV integration, async, ≤ 30 seconds)
   └─ Encrypted at rest immediately upon receipt

4. Pre-Analysis Report (generated within 5 minutes of upload):
   └─ Per-workbook summary:
      - Sheet count and names
      - Estimated row/column counts per sheet
      - Detected formula complexity score (simple/moderate/complex/critical)
      - Cross-sheet reference map
      - External data connection detection (SQL, web, other files)
      - Estimated migration complexity: Green/Yellow/Red
   └─ Overall migration readiness score (0–100)
   └─ Recommended migration sequence (which workbook to import first)

5. Excel Champion reviews pre-analysis report and either:
   a. Proceeds to mapping (Phase 2)
   b. Removes problematic files for manual handling
   c. Requests CSM consultation (triggers CSM task in vendor CRM)
```

**Exit State:** At least one workbook uploaded, scanned, pre-analyzed, and accepted for import by the user.

**Success Gate:** Migration readiness score ≥ 40 OR user has explicitly acknowledged complexity risks and chosen to proceed.

---

#### Phase 2: Schema Mapping (Days 5–10)

**Entry:** Accepted workbook(s) in pre-analyzed state.

**Journey Steps:**

```
1. Smart Import Engine runs automated schema inference (see Section 3)
   └─ Async job; UI shows progress with estimated completion time
   └─ Typical duration: 30 seconds to 5 minutes depending on file complexity

2. Schema Mapping Workspace:
   └─ Left panel: Source columns (from Excel, with sample data)
   └─ Right panel: Target fields (SaaS data model)
   └─ Center: Mapping arrows with confidence indicators
   └─ Color coding:
      GREEN: High-confidence auto-mapped (≥ 85% confidence score)
      YELLOW: Medium-confidence suggestion requiring user confirmation (50–84%)
      RED: Unmapped fields requiring manual assignment or skip decision
      GRAY: Fields the system recommends skipping (low data quality)

3. User reviews and adjusts mappings:
   └─ Drag-to-remap fields
   └─ "Split column" action (e.g., "Full Name" → "First Name" + "Last Name")
   └─ "Concatenate columns" action
   └─ "Derived field" action (simple expressions only in MVP)
   └─ "Skip this column" action (with confirmation: "Data will not be imported")
   └─ "Create custom field" action (adds to target schema)

4. Mapping validation runs in real-time:
   └─ Type compatibility check (text mapped to numeric field: warning)
   └─ Required field completeness check (required target fields with no source)
   └─ Duplicate mapping detection (two source columns → same target field)

5. User saves mapping configuration as a named template
   └─ Template can be reused for subsequent imports of same structure
   └─ Templates are shareable within the organization

6. "Run Preview Import" — imports first 100 rows to validation grid
   └─ User reviews sample data in target format
   └─ Confirms or returns to mapping adjustment
```

**Exit State:** Mapping configuration saved; preview import validated by user.

**Success Gate:** User has clicked "Confirm Mapping" and preview import has zero critical validation errors.

---

#### Phase 3: Full Import & Validation (Days 7–14)

**Entry:** Confirmed mapping configuration.

**Journey Steps:**

```
1. Full import job submitted:
   └─ Async processing; user can leave and return
   └─ Email notification on completion (with deep link to results)
   └─ Progress visible in "My Imports" dashboard

2. Import completes; Validation Report generated:
   └─ Total rows processed
   └─ Rows imported successfully (clean)
   └─ Rows with warnings (imported but flagged)
   └─ Rows with errors (not imported; require correction)
   └─ Breakdown by error type and severity

3. Validation & Error Correction Interface opens (see Section 4)
   └─ User reviews and corrects errors
   └─ Re-submits corrected rows in bulk
